pages.title: How Long Should a Tutoring Session Last?
pages.markdown:
Depending on who you ask, the word “tutoring” could mean a multitude of things. For some, it’s a quick bit of homework help. For others, it’s an every-other-day support system and confidence booster. If you’re just getting started with tutoring, it’s tough to figure out which approach is best. So, how long should a tutoring session last, and how many sessions should you schedule?

It’s no wonder why this is one oof our frequently asked questions!To put it plainly, it depends. Every student is different and has different needs. For those with a greater attention span, you can get away with longer sessions. Longer is not always better though, and some students get more value out of shorter sessions.

**Based on Age, How Long Should Tutoring Sessions Be?**

When kids are younger, they tend to get distracted more easily. Asking them to sit down for any period feels like a lot, so shorter sessions suit them better. Conversely, older students can usually handle working for longer periods of time.

A tutoring session should be **no shorter than 45 minutes**. Less than that isn’t enough time for students to gain new information and internalize it. This is especially true if tutoring is only happening once a week. If your student can’t stay focused for more than 45 minutes, consider having tutoring sessions twice per week.

As your child gets older, you can stretch the tutoring sessions to get more accomplished in a day. This is great if you have a busy schedule because you can have one fully dedicated tutoring day each week. It’s not unheard of to have a three-hour tutoring session, but **two hours is usually a good upper limit.** Extending it too long can sometimes do more harm than good.

For a general guideline, we’ve created an age-based chart to help you get started.

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Grade Level | Session Length | Sessions Per Week |
| K to 5 | 45 minutes to 1 hour | 1 to 2 |
| 6 to 9 | 1 to 1.5 hours | 1 to 3 |
| 10 to 12 | 1 to 2 hours | 1 to 3 |

![](https://www.americangroup-international.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/how-long-should-a-tutoring-session-last-962x656-1.jpg)

**Traditional Schooling vs Homeschooling**

The nature of tutoring will vary depending on whether your child is attending brick-and-mortar school. Make sure you take this into account when scheduling your tutoring sessions. Should they be online or in person.

**Traditional Schooling**

Students attending traditional school can greatly benefit from the extra support a tutor provides. A **one-hour session once per week** is a solid start, but you might want to supplement that with an additional session for best results.

**Homeschooling**

If you’re homeschooling your child, especially if they’re in high school, you’ll want to provide more tutoring time. Consider scheduling **at least two sessions per week**, both anywhere from **one to two hours each**. This will ensure that your student receives the assistance they need.

Tutors can function as teachers, so you can ask them to teach your child’s curriculum. Make sure you allocate enough time to accomplish the goals you would like your tutor to achieve. To simulate a school environment, you can experiment with longer sessions divided by short breaks to improve engagement. **Two-hour or even three-hour sessions** work well in this case.

**Choose a Productive Time of Day**

It’s important to determine how long a tutoring session should last, but you want to make sure the session is during a productive time of day. Conducting a session too late could lead to your child fatiguing and losing interest. If the session is too early, they might not be fully awake yet.

Tutoring sessions **immediately after school** tend to be quite effective. The child will not have settled into the away-from-school mindset just yet, leading to higher levels of focus.

If you’re homeschooling, sessions in the **late morning** and **early afternoon** can maximize your child’s accomplishments. These are peak hours for productivity, giving your student a head-start on success.

**Ask Your Child How Long Should a Tutoring Session Last**

Ultimately, your child is the one receiving the tutoring, so they should have a say in the matter. Check in with them to see what they would like and use that information to plan accordingly. Also, try different times of day to see what works best for them.

**Consult Your Tutor**

Your tutor will get to know your child quite well, and they’ll be able to provide useful information about your child’s habits. Ask for progress reports to see if anything can be adjusted. They’ll let you know if they’re spending too much time trying to keep a lid on things during a long session or if they often wish for more time during shorter ones. Communication is key!

**We Can Help You Decide How Long a Tutoring Session Should Last**

We know tutoring is a big commitment with a ton of variables, so we’re here to support you. Tutoring…With a Twist\* will create a specialized plan that works for you. We’ll guide you through every step of the way and come up with a perfect tutoring schedule for your child. If you’re ready to get started, don’t hesitate to contact us! (agiangliama@gmail.com). We’d love to hear from you!

Thank you for your interest in our Tutor’s.

**Online Applications for Class Instructions for Students and Parents**

Downloading and Accessing Zoom

1. Download Zoom:

   - For Computers: Go to the Zoom website [[zoom.us/download](https://zoom.us/download)](http://zoom.us/download%5D(https:/zoom.us/download)) and click on "Download" under "Zoom Client for Meetings."

   - For Mobile Devices: Search for "Zoom Cloud Meetings" in the App Store (iOS) or Google Play Store (Android) and install the app.

2. Creating an Account:

   - Open the Zoom application.

   - Click "Sign Up" and follow the prompts to create an account using your email address.

3. Joining a Meeting:

   - Open the Zoom application and sign in.

   - Click "Join a Meeting."

   - Enter the Meeting ID and password provided by the teacher.

Downloading and Accessing Microsoft Teams

1. Download Microsoft Teams:

   - For Computers: Go to the Microsoft Teams website [[teams.microsoft.com/downloads](https://teams.microsoft.com/downloads)](http://teams.microsoft.com/downloads%5D(https:/teams.microsoft.com/downloads)) and click "Download for desktop."

   - For Mobile Devices: Search for "Microsoft Teams" in the App Store (iOS) or Google Play Store (Android) and install the app.

2. Creating an Account:

   - Open the Microsoft Teams application.

   - Sign in using your Microsoft account. If you don’t have one, click "Sign Up" and follow the prompts to create an account.

3. Joining a Meeting:

   - Open the Microsoft Teams application and sign in.

   - Click on "Calendar" in the side menu.

   - Click "Join" next to the scheduled meeting.

**Instructions for Teachers**

Scheduling Zoom Meetings

1. Sign in to Zoom:

   - Open the Zoom application or go to [[zoom.us](http://zoom.us/)]([https://zoom.us](https://zoom.us/)) and sign in to your account.

2. Schedule a Meeting:

   - Click "Schedule a Meeting" from the main dashboard.

   - Fill in the meeting details: topic, description, date, time, duration, etc.

   - Adjust the meeting settings as needed (e.g., require a password, enable waiting room).

   - Click "Save."

3. Share Meeting Details:

   - After scheduling the meeting, you will see the meeting details page.

   - Click "Copy the Invitation" and share the meeting ID and password with the students via email or your preferred communication method.

Scheduling Microsoft Teams Meetings

1. Sign in to Microsoft Teams:

   - Open the Microsoft Teams application or go to [[teams.microsoft.com](http://teams.microsoft.com/)]([https://teams.microsoft.com](https://teams.microsoft.com/)) and sign in to your account.

2. Schedule a Meeting:

   - Click on "Calendar" in the side menu.

   - Click "New Meeting" at the top right corner.

   - Fill in the meeting details: title, participants, date, time, and description.

   - Adjust the meeting options as needed (e.g., require lobby, enable meeting chat).

   - Click "Save."

3. Share Meeting Details:

   - Once the meeting is scheduled, you will see it in your calendar.

   - Click on the meeting and select "Share via email" or copy the meeting link and share it with the students.

**Directions and Scheduling for Students and Parents**

1. Weekly Schedule:

   - The teacher will provide a weekly schedule with the days and times of each tutoring session.

   - Ensure you have the correct meeting links, IDs, and passwords for each session.

2. Preparing for the Session:

   - Make sure your device (computer, tablet, or phone) is charged and has a stable internet connection.

   - Log in to Zoom or Microsoft Teams a few minutes before the session starts to ensure everything is working properly.

   - Have any necessary materials (books, notebooks, pens) ready before the session begins.

3. During the Session:

   - Join the meeting at the scheduled time using the provided meeting link.

   - Participate actively and complete any assignments or activities as instructed by the tutor.

   - Ask questions if you need clarification on any topics.

4. After the Session:

   - Review the session's materials and complete any homework or practice activities assigned by the tutor.

   - Reach out to the teacher via email or messaging if you have any questions or need further assistance.

By following these directions, both students and teachers can ensure smooth and productive tutoring sessions.

# C.I.T.E - Certificate for International Teachers of English (TESOL)

**Enhance your teaching skills and gain recognition for your proficiency with the prestigious C.I.T.E. certification offered by Anglia Examinations England. This lifelong qualification demonstrates your mastery of English and your ability to teach the language effectively. Register now to elevate your teaching career!**

## What is C.I.T.E?

**C.I.T.E.** (Certificate  for International Teachers of English) is a prestigious **TESOL** qualification offered by Anglia Examinations England. This certification demonstrates your mastery of English and your ability to teach the language effectively. It's a lifelong qualification with no expiration date, recognized worldwide.

### Who is C.I.T.E. for?

**The C.I.T.E. test recognizes your competence in English language skills necessary for teaching. It is suitable for:**

- ##### Current English Teachers

  Validate and enhance your English teaching skills.

- ##### Aspiring Teachers

  Start your teaching career with a recognized certification.

- ##### High School Teachers

  Add English teaching to your skill set.

- ##### Primary School Teachers

  Meet new curriculum requirements with confidence.

### **How to Register**

1. **Determine Your English Level**: Visit [**www.angliaonline.com**](http://www.angliaonline.com) or schedule an appointment with an authorized Anglia partner.
2. **Register Online**: [[Register Here]](#)
3. **Payment and Confirmation**: After registration, you will be contacted via email to arrange payment for the examination.

### Prepare for Success

Anglia Morocco offers the necessary training and resources to help you succeed. Recommended books include:

- ***Brown, H. Douglas. Principles of Language Learning and Teaching. Prentice Hall Regents, 2000.***
- ***Brown, Douglas H. Teaching by Principles: An Interactive Approach to Language Pedagogy. Prentice Hall Regents, 2001.***
- ***Harmer, Jeremy. The Practice of English Language Teaching. Longman, 1983.***
- ***Hewings, Martin. Advanced Grammar in Use. Cambridge University Press, 2005.***
- ***Ioannou-Georgiou, Sophie, and Pavlos Pavlou. Assessing Young Learners. Oxford University Press, 2003.***
- ***Slattery, Mary, and Jane Willis. English for Primary Teachers. Oxford University Press, 2001.***
- ***Vale, D., and A. Feunteun. Teaching Children English. Cambridge University Press, 1995.***

### Examination Process

- **Format**: Paper format at Anglia partnerships in Morocco or online via the Anglia Examinations UK Portal.
- **Duration**: The C.I.T.E test lasts 3 hours.
- **Guidance**: Candidates will receive login details and a guide prior to the exam session.

### Results and Certificates

- **Results**: 5-6 weeks after tests are received at the control centre in Chichester, England.
- **Certificates**: Up to 8 weeks after completion of testing.
- Results will be sent electronically to the email provided during the application.

## Why Choose Anglia C.I.T.E.?

**No Entry Requirements**

**Inclusive Approach:**The C.I.T.E. certification is accessible to all, regardless of prior qualifications, making it ideal for both current and aspiring English teachers.

**Flexible Levels:** Candidates can choose the level that best suits their needs, from C.I.T.E. Master to versions tailored for young and very young learners.

**Lifelong Qualification**

**Permanent Certification:** Once earned, the C.I.T.E. certification is valid for life, providing lasting value without the need for renewal.

**Recognition and Accreditation**

**Internationally Recognized:** The C.I.T.E. certification is respected worldwide, ensuring your qualifications are valued by educational institutions and employers globally.

**Accredited Standards:** Anglia Examinations England ensures that the C.I.T.E. certification meets high standards of quality and rigor.

**Practical Focus**

**Teaching Competence:** The C.I.T.E. certification demonstrates your proficiency in essential English language skills needed for effective teaching.

**Diverse Application:** Suitable for a wide range of teaching contexts, from primary schools to high schools, and for teachers with varied backgrounds.

**Comprehensive Preparation**

**Support and Training:** Anglia Morocco offers extensive preparatory support, including practice exams and recommended reading materials.

**Professional Development:** The certification process and associated resources help enhance your teaching skills and knowledge.

**Flexible Examination Options**

**Convenient Testing:** Choose to take the C.I.T.E. test in paper format at Anglia partnerships in Morocco, at the headquarters in Agadir, or online through the Anglia Examinations UK Portal.

### **Accreditation and Recognition**

### Accreditation

The C.I.T.E. (Certificate for International Teachers of English) is accredited by Anglia Examinations England, a recognized body in the UK that ensures the highest standards of quality and rigor in English language teaching certifications.

### Recognition

**Privacy Statement**

At American Group International Prive /Anglia Morocco in Agadir, Morocco we are committed to safeguarding and preserving the privacy of our visitors.

This Privacy Policy explains what happens to any personal data that you provide to us, or that we collect from you whilst you visit our site.

We do update this Policy from time to time so please do review this Policy regularly.

**Information We Collect**

In running and maintaining our website we may collect and process the following data about you:

1. Information about your use of our site including details of your visits such as pages viewed and the resources that you access. Such information includes traffic data, location data and other communication data.
2. Information provided voluntarily by you. For example, when you register for information.
3. Information that you provide when you communicate with us by any means.

**Use of Cookies**

Cookies provide information regarding the computer used by a visitor. We may use cookies where appropriate to gather information about your computer in order to assist us in improving our website.

We may gather information about your general internet use by using the cookie.  Where used, these cookies are downloaded to your computer and stored on the computer’s hard drive. Such information will not identify you personally. It is statistical data. This statistical data does not identify any personal details whatsoever

You can adjust the settings on your computer to decline any cookies if you wish.  This can easily be done by activating the reject cookies setting on your computer.

**Use of Your Information**

We use the information that we collect from you to provide our services to you.  In addition to this we may use the information for one or more of the following purposes:

1. To provide information to you that you request from us relating to our programs or services.
2. To provide information to you relating to other information that may be of interest to you.

**Storing Your Personal Data**

In operating our website, it may become necessary to transfer data that we collect from you to our data warehouse locations for processing and storing. By providing your personal data to us, you agree to this transfer, storing or processing. We do our utmost to ensure that all reasonable steps are taken to make sure that your data is treated and stored securely.

Unfortunately the sending of information via the internet is not totally secure and on occasion such information can be intercepted. We cannot guarantee the security of data that you choose to send us electronically, sending such information is entirely at your own risk.

**Disclosing Your Information**

We will not disclose your personal information to any other party other than in accordance with this Privacy Policy and in the circumstances detailed below:

1. Where we are legally required by law to disclose your personal information.
2. To further fraud protection and reduce the risk of fraud.

**Third Party Links**On occasion we include links to third parties on this website. Where we provide a link, it does not mean that we endorse or approve that site’s policy towards visitor privacy. You should review their privacy policy before sending them any personal data.

We do not request or store credit card information. All online payments are done through third party dedicated and secure sites, e.g. Maroc Telecommerce or PayPal. Please see their website for their privacy policy.

**Contacting Us**

Please do not hesitate to contact us regarding any matter relating to this Privacy Policy at: americanecoleagadir@gmail.com or contact our webmaster.

American Group International (AGI) is proud to announce that as of Spring 2026, the organization is officially recognized as a partner of the American School Counselor Association (ASCA) in the United States through its Principal and Founder, Julie Wilburn.

The American School Counselor Association (ASCA), founded in 1952, is the leading professional organization for school counselors in the U.S. ASCA sets the standard for student counseling programs by providing ethical guidelines, professional development, research, and a nationally recognized framework known as the ASCA National Model. The association advocates for comprehensive academic, college, and career guidance and supports student well-being and success.

Through this partnership, AGI strengthens its mission to provide professional, research-based guidance and counseling support to students in Morocco and internationally. L’American School Counselor Association (ASCA), fondée en 1952, est l’organisation professionnelle de référence pour les conseillers scolaires aux États-Unis. # Celebrating Excellence with Our Partner

## American High School – Yass Prize Awardee

At **American Group International (AGI)**, we take immense pride in celebrating the outstanding achievements of our partner, **American High School (AHS)**. Their recognition as a distinguished **Yass Prize Awardee** reflects their visionary leadership, innovative educational model, and unwavering commitment to empowering learners across diverse communities.

This milestone is more than an award — it is a testament to AHS’s transformative impact and the shared mission we proudly uphold together: expanding access, opportunity, and excellence in education.

### What Makes This Achievement Exceptional

- **Educational Innovation:** AHS is redefining modern learning with flexible, student‑centered pathways.
- **Impactful Reach:** Their programs uplift underserved, marginalized, and justice‑involved learners.
- **Leadership in Equity:** AHS sets a national standard for inclusive, high‑quality education.
- **Shared Vision:** AGI is honored to partner with an institution that aligns with our mission of global educational advancement.

Join us in congratulating American High School on this remarkable accomplishment.

 [Learn More About Their Achievement](https://yassprize.org/awardees/american-high-school)

## American High School – Yass Prize (Embedded)

View the original American High School page from the Yass Prize website directly below:

If the embedded page does not display,  [click here to open it in a new tab.](https://yassprize.org/awardees/american-high-school)

## About American High School

American High School is an innovative education network founded in 2004. It supports incarcerated, marginalized, and justice‑involved learners by offering accredited high school diplomas and career‑focused certifications. Programs operate in juvenile detention centers, reentry initiatives, and underserved communities, helping students reconnect with education and build stronger futures.

Through trauma‑informed teaching, flexible scheduling, and individualized pathways, American High School works to remove barriers to learning. Students gain both academic credentials and practical skills that prepare them for employment, additional training, or further education, creating real opportunities for long‑term success.

### Key focus areas

- **Accredited diplomas:** High school completion for students who have been pushed out of traditional systems.
- **Career certifications:** Training that connects learners to real job opportunities and trades.
- **Justice‑involved youth:** Programs tailored for incarcerated and reentering students.
- **Trauma‑informed approach:** Educators trained to support students with complex life experiences.
- **Flexible learning:** Schedules and pathways that adapt to students’ realities.

## 

## **Chichester College Group International**

## **(CCGi) – Overview**

### **A Leader in International Education**

CCGi is the international arm of Chichester College Group (CCG), which has been rated 'Outstanding' by Ofsted, the UK’s education standards authority.

The group comprises seven colleges across ten campuses across West Sussex and Brighton & Hove.

Mission & Reputation

### CCGi’s mission: “Changing lives through learning.”.

Recognized for academic excellence and comprehensive student support—especially for international learners.

### **Key Programs Offered**

English Language Courses: General English (15 & 21), delivered via the British Council-accredited Chichester English Language School, ranked among the top 5% in the UK.

A-Levels & AS-Levels: Two-year A-Levels at Chichester and Worthing; one-year AS-Levels at Worthing.

Vocational Courses & BTECs: Practical, skills-focused courses in areas like hospitality, engineering, health & social care, creative arts.

University Foundation Programs: Pathways ensuring progression to UK or international universities.

Higher Education Degrees: Undergraduate degrees (HNC, HND, level 4–6) in fields like business, engineering, art, media, motorsport, animal management, music, sports, teaching—accredited by institutions such as University of the Arts London (UAL) and University of Brighton.

Study Abroad, Winter/Summer Schools: Short-term immersive experiences combining academics with British cultural activities.

### **Student Support & Unique Experience**

Comprehensive services: Visa guidance, accommodation assistance (homestays, halls), welfare, enrichment and social activities.

Highly equipped campuses: State-of-the-art facilities including farms, animal care centres, equine training, workshops, labs, and creative arts studios.

Cultural immersion: Organized trips to iconic UK sites like London, Oxford, Stonehenge, fostering personal growth and global citizenship.

Global student body: Enrols students from regions including East Asia, Europe, and beyond.

### **Strategic Partnerships & Agents Network**

CCGi maintains partnerships with academic institutions, awarding bodies, and global agents who represent them locally to prospective students.

Strategic collaborations include organisations like NOCN, supporting qualification accreditation.

#### Spotlight on CCGi Colleges

1. Chichester College

Main campus in Chichester, plus Brinsbury (agricultural campus with a working farm and animal care facilities) .

Offers A-Levels, BTECs, vocational programs, and some university-level courses.

2. Northbrook College

Based in Worthing with campuses in West Durrington and Shoreham-by-Sea (campus sale planned in 2025) .

Strong in creative and cultural higher education: fashion, photography, media (validated by UAL), plus motorsport engineering (via University of Brighton) .

3. Worthing College

Sixth-form college in Worthing offering A-Levels & AS-Levels; also, part of CCG’s broader vocational and international portfolio.

4. Brighton MET College

Former Brighton MET (merged August 2021); campuses in central and east Brighton.

Offers trades, technical subjects, adult education, and visual arts progression.

5. Crawley College and Haywards Heath College

Additional FE/Higher Education providers under the CCG umbrella—extending geographic range and offerings.

6. Brinsbury

Specialized land-based and agricultural centre; integral to Chichester College’s offerings.

American Group International is a proud partner of CCGi and we will be working on projects and educational programs to help the local Moroccan community.

This impactful event brought together educational institutions, international partners, and passionate educators—all committed to enhancing English language education throughout Morocco and promoting English as a medium of instruction in various academic disciplines.

Anglia in Morocco has been extremely active in the community this month. We have taken the final  
steps and put a salesman in place in the Casablanca area.

Rachid Oussalh’s BIO is attached  
here…

![](http://www.americangroup-international.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/image-1024x1024.png)

I am currently working as a Teacher  
of English at Max Weber Academy  
in Dar Bouazza. I did my English  
Linguistic Studies at the universities  
of Ibn Zohr in Agadir and at Hassan  
II in Casablanca.  
I also got several certifications such  
as TKT, FCE, CAE, Child  
Protection, Safety & Security, and  
more from the British Council  
Morocco and in the United  
Kingdom, Italy, Egypt, Libya, and  
Jordan.  
I am so excited to be part of the  
Anglia community as a Representative here in Casablanca and to help students, teachers, and  
those interested in getting Anglia internationally recognized certificates and diplomas.  
I have been working in the English learning environment for over twenty years now; first as a  
teacher of English in Agadir, then as a Resources and Admin Officer at the British Council,  
then at George Washington Academy as the General Services Manager.  
During my tenure at the British Council, I managed to launch and administer the TKT  
(Teacher Knowledge Test) and the CELTA courses among the English Department students  
and the teachers of English at the private schools. I also attended several book and education  
fairs to promote the IELTS and the Cambridge exams such as KET, PET. FCE. and CAE.  
It is certainly an honour to become the salesman for Anglia, Morocco and to work with Ms  
Julie A. Wilburn who is leading a successful educational project in Morocco and  
particularly in the town of Agadir and its regions.  
We are currently in discussion about four bigger projects and are working to bring them to  
the reality. Anglia is on the move in Morocco.

news.markdown:
HISTORY OF SOI

### ***American Group International has partnered with Energia SOI to bring one of the best cognitive programs for children and young adults.  Programs are customized for students with Reading and Math difficulties.***

### ***[Learning Math (Funny)](http://www.americangroup-international.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/Learning-Math-Funny.wmv)***

[video width="1280" height="720" mp4="http://www.americangroup-international.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/ENERGIA-SOI-INTRODUCTION-02112016.mp4"][/video]

### "EDUCATION IS NOT THE LEARNING OF FACTS, BUT THE TRAINING OF THE MIND TO THINK"

##### -ALBERT EINSTEIN

Dr. J.P. Guilford was an American Psychologist best remembered for his psychometric study of human intelligence, including the distinction between convergent and divergent production. A Review of General Psychology survey, published in 2002, ranked Guilford as the 27th most cited psychologist of the 20th century.  
  
Our story starts back during World War II when about 35% of pilots were failing out of the Air Corps. These men had IQs over 120, but they still weren’t making it.  
It became Dr. J.P. Guilford’s job to find a new way of measuring intelligence. Guilford drew up sets of intellectual functions required for the various Army Corps jobs and constructed tests that measured those abilities.  
  
Guildford’s tests were used to select personnel with the most intellectual potential for training, and the washout rate dropped by more than 25 percent!  
Pleased with Guilford’s great success, the Defense Department-funded Guilford for the next twenty years in the Aptitudes Project at the University of Southern California.  
  
He and his students continued to identify many different abilities, and a model began to take shape. That model became the Structure of Intellect.  
  
Our founder, Dr. Mary Meeker, was one of Guilford’s students. She saw the potential of the model, especially for identifying learning difficulties. Dr. Meeker soon discovered that certain intellectual abilities were related to basic learning: reading, arithmetic, higher math, creativity, and more.  
  
Dr. Meeker’s most exciting and important contribution was her realization that intellectual abilities could be taught! This added a whole new dimension to Guilford’s work.  
  
At this point, not only could abilities be identified, but they could be taught and developed, too! This coupling is what makes SOI unique. It provides the basis of all our tests, products, and programs that have been developed by Dr. Meeker and her husband, Dr. Robert Meeker.  
  
SOI Systems was officially founded in 1965. And here we are today, more than 50 years later, continuing to impact lives and make a difference, all thanks to the research and development of such a powerful learning system!

news.title: Online Classes for Language Students starting in June 2020.
news.markdown:
## **What is an online/virtual classroom???**

![](http://www.americangroup-international.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/05/cfd86ae1-0a30-40d0-9d7b-3d5bf182bef6-1024x682.jpg)

A virtual classroom is a digital replica of a traditional classroom or training room. The instructors teach, and the participants learn in real-time, face-to-face but via internet-enabled technology devices. The classroom or the meeting room staple – whiteboard – remains intact. Brainstorming, idealization, and discussions happen in real-time. Tests are given and taken pre and post the session. The reports are ready right after the session is over.

Everything remains the way it is. The only difference is: an online classroom uses technology to support instruction and learning. What are the advantages of a virtual classroom? It offers more flexibility over a traditional classroom. You can deliver the instruction to a geographically dispersed audience at one time. Both the instructors and learners have rich experience of collaborating with other learners and instructors from around the world. The attendance is automatically tracked. Moreover, online collaboration typically incorporates more communication tools, such as chat, open discussion boards, polls, multimedia content, and social media.

The **online class software** works in a similar fashion for businesses. You can train employees, vendors, partners, and customers face-to-face in real-time via a standalone app or you can also integrate it with your website, CMS, ERP, or LMS. You can conduct the training even when the stakeholders are on the move. They can access the e-Learning material and attend the live session from their smartphones, tablets, or laptops.

Teacher Training Program Assistant:
Work under a teacher’s supervision to give students additional attention and instruction.
Duties
Teacher assistants typically do the following:

Reinforce lessons presented by teachers by reviewing material with students one-on-one or in small groups
Enforce school and class rules to help teach students proper behavior
Help teachers with record keeping, such as tracking attendance and calculating grades
Help teachers prepare for lessons by getting materials ready or setting up equipment, such as computers
Help supervise students in class, between classes, during lunch and recess, and on field trips
Teacher assistants also are called teacher aides, instructional aides, paraprofessionals, education assistants and para-educators.
Generally, teachers introduce new material to students, and teacher assistants help reinforce the lessons by working with individual students or small groups of students. For example, after the teacher presents a lesson, a teacher assistant may help a small group of students as they try to master the material.
Teachers may seek feedback from assistants to monitor students’ progress. Some teachers and teacher assistants meet regularly to discuss lesson plans and student development. Teacher assistants sometimes help teachers by grading tests and checking homework.
Some teacher assistants work only with special education students. These students often attend regular classes, and teacher assistants help them understand the material and adapt the information to their learning style.
With students who have more severe disabilities, assistants may work with them in separate classes. Teacher assistants help these students with basic needs, such as eating or personal hygiene. With young adults, they may help students with disabilities learn skills necessary for them to find a job or live independently after graduation.
Some teacher assistants work in specific locations in the school. For example, some work in computer laboratories, teaching students how to use computers and helping them use software. Others work as recess or lunchroom attendants, supervising students during these times of the day.
Although most teacher assistants work in elementary, middle, and high schools, others work in preschools and childcare centers. Often, one or two assistants work with a lead teacher to provide the individual attention that young children need. They help with educational activities. They also supervise the children at play and help with feeding and other basic care.

Nous fournissons ce service à un coût très modeste qui comprend tout le soutien nécessaire pour assurer le succès; assistance tutorale, et des services après l'obtention du diplôme tels que l'inscription officielle ou la vérification de l'obtention du diplôme; des lettres de recommandation à des tiers autorisés, et des relevés de notes officiels au nom des diplômés qui cherchent à poursuivre des études supérieures.![](http://www.americangroup-international.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/04/B9323964751Z.1_20160924224133_000_GFFFQS28R.1-0.jpg)**
